turns.Question: Find the positions and intensities of the 7 major Raman peaks in the input polystyrene spectrum. Input file(s): T042.csv.
turns.Ans:
Based on the analysis of the polystyrene Raman spectrum provided in file **T042.csv**, the positions and intensities of the 7 major peaks are as follows:

| Peak | Position ($\text{cm}^{-1}$) | Intensity (a.u.) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| 1 | 620.00 | 460.45 |
| 2 | 1001.00 | 1061.76 |
| 3 | 1031.00 | 629.25 |
| 4 | 1155.00 | 263.20 |
| 5 | 1450.00 | 442.04 |
| 6 | 1583.00 | 427.26 |
| 7 | 1602.00 | 690.76 |

The most intense peak is located at **$1001\text{ cm}^{-1}$**, which corresponds to the characteristic ring-breathing mode of the polystyrene aromatic rings.

args.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks

# Load data
file = files[0]
x = file['table']['raman_shift_cm-1']
y = file['table']['intensity']

# Plot original spectrum
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(x, y, label='Original Spectrum')
plt.xlabel('Raman Shift (cm-1)')
plt.ylabel('Intensity')
plt.title('Polystyrene Raman Spectrum - T042')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)

# Peak detection: looking for major peaks
# Polystyrene usually has high intensity sharp peaks. 
# I'll use a height threshold to filter out noise and look for the top 7.
peaks, properties = find_peaks(y, height=100, distance=20)
peak_pos = x[peaks]
peak_int = y[peaks]

# Sort peaks by intensity and take top 7
idx = np.argsort(peak_int)[::-1]
top_7_idx = idx[:7]

final_peaks_pos = peak_pos[top_7_idx]
final_peaks_int = peak_int[top_7_idx]

# Sort by position for cleaner reporting
sort_by_pos = np.argsort(final_peaks_pos)
final_peaks_pos = final_peaks_pos[sort_by_pos]
final_peaks_int = final_peaks_int[sort_by_pos]

plt.plot(final_peaks_pos, final_peaks_int, "x", color='red', label='Major Peaks')
plt.legend()
plt.savefig('polystyrene_peaks.png')

print("Detected Top 7 Peaks:")
for p, i in zip(final_peaks_pos, final_peaks_int):
    print(f"Position: {p:.2f} cm-1, Intensity: {i:.2f}")
